nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist * [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. * [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) for this project. * [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.6 (25G72) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Calling `webview.findInPage()` should return search results and keep the Electron application responsive. ### Actual Behavior A minimal Electron app becomes unresponsive after calling native `webview.findInPage()` when the same window contains an iframe. The call returns synchronously, but no `found-in-page` event arrives and the app stops processing its event loop. The user-visible result is a complete application hang. The attached reproduction searches for the single-character query `a`, but the same behavior occurs while rapidly navigating matches with Enter. The behavior reproduces with ordinary web pages as well as Google Docs. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/taozhou-glean/54bad8ed029baf3ef99f5a8f7ce7a560 ### Additional Information
In-depth investigation

I reproduced this in a clean Electron 44.4.3 app using one host-page iframe and one webview. The host iframe is intentionally tiny and hidden; removing it avoids the repro in the tested environment. The gist uses data URLs and does not depend on a specific website. Environment: - Electron 44.4.3 - Chromium 152.0.7977.130 - macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64, Mac15,7 - Electron process launched from Ghostty During the hang, a macOS sample reported the Electron main process unresponsive for 40 seconds. The main process used 4.116 seconds of CPU in a 4.20-second sampled interval and had a 352 MB footprint. Symbolicating Electron Framework 44.4.3 identified the repeated path as: ```text content::FindRequestManager::FinalUpdateReceived(int, content::RenderFrameHost*) content::FindRequestManager::Traverse(content::RenderFrameHost*, bool, bool, bool) content::(anonymous namespace)::GetChildren(content::RenderFrameHostImpl*) content::(anonymous namespace)::GetNextSibling(content::RenderFrameHostImpl*) ``` This appears to be the same class of issue described in [electron/electron#20602](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/20602), where a comment reports an infinite loop in `find_request_manager.cc` with a webview and iframe. That issue is closed, and the problem remains reproducible on Electron 44.4.3. A renderer-side `window.find()` implementation does not hang on the same fixture, which further isolates the failure to the native Electron/Chromium find-in-page path.

— sent via Glean Tau

nodes.title: Linux tray registers a hollow StatusNotifierItem on Electron 43 (no interfaces exported)
nodes.body:
## Environment

- Electron: 43 (Arch Linux system package `/usr/lib/electron43`, Chromium with the StatusNotifierItem multiplexer refactor crrev.com/c/8043132)
- OS: Linux (Hyprland/Wayland session, dbus session bus)
- Also reproduced on: same runtime via `electron43 --no-sandbox`

## Repro

```js
// main.js
const { app, Tray, nativeImage } = require("electron");
app.whenReady().then(() => {
    const img = nativeImage.createFromPath("/path/to/any.png"); // valid 225x225 png, img.isEmpty() === false
    const tray = new Tray(img);
    tray.setToolTip("tray-probe");
});
```

Run with `electron43 main.js`.

## Expected

The tray exports `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` with Properties (IconName/IconPixmap/ToolTip/...) at its object path, like Electron <= 42.

## Actual

- The app acquires `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` and registers with the watcher (`RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` gains `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem`).
- The object at `/StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem` exists but is an **empty node**: no `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` interface, no `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties` (`gdbus introspect` returns `node /StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem {};`, property Get fails with `Method \"Get\" ... doesn't exist`).
- It never fills in — the item stays hollow for the app's entire lifetime.
- The same pattern is visible in long-running apps: GoofCord (open source, `new Tray(png); tray.setToolTip()` — nothing exotic) sits in the tray as an image-missing placeholder forever on Electron 43, while the same apps work with older Electron builds (Signal/Ferdium ship their own).

Verbose startup logging (`--enable-logging --v=1`) shows the dbus layer retrying during init (`GetNameOwner` storm, `Filter function already exists`), and name ownership takes ~15s instead of being immediate; no `RequestName`/`RegisterStatusNotifierItem` method calls are visible in the `dbus/bus.cc` method-call trace, suggesting the multiplexer/registration path runs somewhere the verbose log doesn't cover.

## Impact

Any Electron-43 app using `Tray` on Linux shows a broken/placeholder tray icon in StatusNotifierItem hosts (tested against AstalTray's watcher). The registration also never gets reaped when the app dies because it is keyed by the combined name/path string (reported separately to AstalTray as Aylur/astal#485, now with a known producer).

Happy to run any diagnostics against the live system.

Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.2.6-1-cachyos, x86_64, KDE Plasma on Wayland ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Dropping a file onto a window fires the `drop` event and the application receives the file, regardless of what characters the file's name contains. ### Actual Behavior If the dropped file's **name** contains a non-ASCII character (tested with U+2014 EM DASH), the Electron process dies immediately with **SIGTRAP**. No `dragenter`, `dragover` or `drop` handler ever runs, and nothing is logged. A byte-identical copy of the same file with an ASCII-only name is dropped and handled normally, so the file's contents, size and format are not involved — only its name. Tested in both directions repeatedly; it is 100% consistent. Chromium 152 on the same machine, with an equivalent drop target on a local page, accepts the same em-dash file without any problem. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information **Minimal reproduction** (three files): `package.json` ```json { "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js", "private": true } ``` `main.js` ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const w = new BrowserWindow({ width: 760, height: 520, webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false } }); w.loadFile('index.html'); }); app.on('window-all-closed', () => app.quit()); ``` `index.html` ```html
drop a file here
``` Steps: 1. `touch "repro — test.md"` — the separator is U+2014 EM DASH (bytes `e2 80 94`). 2. `cp "repro — test.md" repro-test.md` 3. `npm i electron && ./node_modules/.bin/electron .` 4. Drag `repro-test.md` onto the window → logs `dropped repro-test.md`. Works. 5. Drag `repro — test.md` onto the window → the process exits with SIGTRAP; no handler runs.
In-depth investigation

systemd-coredump for the crash in the minimal app above: ``` Signal: 5 (TRAP) si_code: SI_KERNEL Stack trace of thread 60221 (main thread): #0 0x0000562ad9e364c0 n/a (electron + 0x839c4c0) #1 0x0000562ad9f889ee n/a (electron + 0x84ee9ee) #2 0x0000562ad9f895c6 n/a (electron + 0x84ef5c6) #3 0x0000562ada045484 n/a (electron + 0x85ab484) #4 0x0000562ada156245 n/a (electron + 0x86bc245) #5 0x0000562ada155fcb n/a (electron + 0x86bbfcb) #6 0x0000562ada155e65 n/a (electron + 0x86bbe65) ``` (unsymbolized — stock stripped release binary) I originally hit this in Discord 1.0.158, which ships Electron 42.11.1: attaching any file with an em dash in its name kills the client instantly, before the upload begins (its `renderer_js.log` shows no `CloudUpload` entry for the failing file, while ASCII-named files in the same session log the normal upload sequence). Discord's Crashpad dumps show the same signature — `SIGTRAP` at `0x0`, `ptype=utility` — with `libgtk-3`, `libgdk-3`, `libgdk_pixbuf-2.0`, `libglycin-2` and `libtinysparql-3.0` loaded in the crashing process. Because of that module list I first suspected the known gdk-pixbuf ≥ 2.44.1 / glycin / `bwrap` crash class (GNOME/gdk-pixbuf#292), where a failing glycin loader leads to a fatal GTK assertion. That appears **not** to be it: `app.getFileIcon()` resolves the same em-dash paths without error (tested on both the `.md` and a `.pdf`), so the icon/thumbnail path is not implicated. Environment: gtk3 1:3.24.52, gdk-pixbuf2 2.44.7, glycin 2.1.5, bubblewrap 0.12.0, xdg-desktop-portal 1.22.1 with both -gtk 1.15.3 and -kde 6.7.5 installed. Not tested: X11, other distributions, other non-ASCII codepoints (only U+2014 so far).

nodes.title: Tray icon does not visually update on GNOME while the app is unfocused (NewIcon signal fires correctly)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.7.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1 (Wayland session; app launched with `--ozone-platform=x11`) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ - not a regression as far as I can tell, seems to affect this Electron version and possibly others. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior After calling `tray.setImage()` with a new icon while the app's `BrowserWindow` is unfocused, the tray icon in the top panel updates immediately, the same as it does when the app is focused. ### Actual Behavior The tray icon often stays on the previous image while the app is unfocused, and only catches up once the window regains focus (or some other event forces GNOME Shell to repaint the top panel). ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/oalfroukh/5a3d7677823db53c9b4b05c2d3ced221 ### Additional Information Run the gist with `electron . --ozone-platform=x11`. It creates a window, waits 3s, blurs the window, waits 1s, then calls `tray.setImage()` with a different (red) icon while `win.isFocused()` is `false`. On GNOME Shell with the `ubuntu-appindicators` extension, the icon frequently does not turn red until the window is refocused.
In-depth investigation

I ran `dbus-monitor --session "interface='org.kde.StatusNotifierItem'"` alongside the repro and confirmed Electron emits `NewIconThemePath` and `NewIcon` on the `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` interface correctly every time `tray.setImage()` is called, including while the window is unfocused - captured a signal timestamped well after `win.isFocused()` was already `false`. `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` on `IconName` also reflects the new icon name immediately, unfocused or not. So Electron's side of the StatusNotifierItem protocol appears correct in both the signal and the property value. The GNOME `ubuntu-appindicators` extension (https://github.com/ubuntu/gnome-shell-extension-appindicator) seems to not always repaint the panel icon in response to `NewIcon` alone while the associated window is unfocused, though I haven't dug into that extension's source to confirm why. I'm filing this against Electron rather than the extension because: this pattern (GNOME AppIndicator/StatusNotifierItem quirks) has come up in several Electron issues before (#52674, #53213, #53138), so the team may already be aware of extension-side flakiness like this, and may know of a workaround Electron could apply (e.g. re-emitting the icon signals on focus/blur, or another pattern that happens to be more reliable against this consumer) even though the root cause is outside Electron's own code.

Support macOS system Password AutoFill providers for HTML credential fields
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

On macOS, standard HTML username/password fields in an Electron application do not appear to participate in the system Password AutoFill experience, even when a credential provider is configured at the OS level.

For example, given:

```html
<input
  type="text"
  name="username"
  autocomplete="username"
/>

<input
  type="password"
  name="password"
  autocomplete="current-password"
/>
```
the same page produces different behavior depending on where it is rendered:

Environment | Result
-- | --
Safari, macOS AutoFill provider configured | System Password AutoFill offered the configured provider
Chrome, provider's browser extension enabled | Browser extension offered credentials
Chrome, browser extension disabled | No system Password AutoFill suggestion
Electron | No system AutoFill suggestion

*These tests were performed with 1Password as the configured macOS AutoFill provider*

In this test, Electron did not provide the native macOS Password AutoFill experience that Safari provided for the same semantic HTML fields.

This came up while using pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is an Electron application. 1Password Universal Autofill (Cmd+\) works there, but the native inline Password AutoFill experience does not.


### Proposed Solution

Electron apps should be able to use macOS Password AutoFill for standard username and password fields without requiring a browser extension.

For example, fields using standard HTML attributes such as:

```
autocomplete="username"
autocomplete="current-password"
```
should be able to show credentials from password managers configured in macOS, similar to how the same fields behave in Safari.

I’m not sure whether this should be handled in Electron or upstream in Chromium. I’m opening this issue to confirm whether this is something Electron intends to support and, if so, where the change should be made.


### Alternatives Considered

#### 1Password Universal Autofill

In pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is a signed Electron application, 1Password Universal Autofill using Cmd+\ can fill the credential field. This works, but it is a separate workflow from macOS's native inline Password AutoFill experience and requires the user to know and invoke the shortcut.

#### Browser extensions

When the application is run in Chrome, the 1Password browser extension provides autofill. Electron applications, however, cannot generally rely on users installing browser password-manager extensions.

#### Application-specific password-manager integration

Individual Electron applications could potentially integrate with password managers themselves, but that would require each application to implement provider-specific behavior rather than using the operating system's credential-provider mechanism.

### Additional Information

Minimal test field:

```html
<form>
  <label>
    Username
    <input
      type="text"
      name="username"
      autocomplete="username"
    />
  </label>

  <label>
    Password
    <input
      type="password"
      name="password"
      autocomplete="current-password"
    />
  </label>
</form>
```
Minimal Electron wrapper used for the reproduction:
```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

function createWindow() {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 600,
    height: 400,
  });

  win.loadURL('http://127.0.0.1:8080');
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true);
  createWindow();

  app.on('activate', () => {
    if (BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length === 0) {
      createWindow();
    }
  });
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => {
  if (process.platform !== 'darwin') {
    app.quit();
  }
});
```
I also reproduced the behavior without `app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true);` enabling it explicitly did not change the Password AutoFill behavior.

Tested on:
```
macOS: 26.5.1 (Tahoe, 25F80)
Electron: 44.4.3
Architecture: arm64
1Password: 8.12.36 (81236040)
Safari: 26.5 (21624.2.5.11.4)
Chrome: 152.0.7977.84 (Official Build) (arm64)
```

<details> 
<summary>In-depth investigation</summary>
I originally encountered this with pgAdmin 4 Desktop and compared its behavior with pgAdmin 4 running in a normal browser.

Accessibility Inspector shows that Electron exposes the password field to macOS as a secure text field:
```
Role: AXTextField
Subrole: AXSecureTextField
Class: BrowserAccessibilityCocoa
```

A minimal Electron test application exposes its password field with the same accessibility role/subrole.

I also tested:
- Electron loaded from `file://`
- Electron loading the same page over `http://127.0.0.1`
- `app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true)`
- a packaged Electron application

The packaged test application was ad-hoc signed. 1Password Universal Autofill did not fill it, which is consistent with 1Password's requirement for a trusted code signature. pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is normally signed, does support 1Password Universal Autofill via `Cmd+\`.

This suggests the accessibility representation and 1Password Universal Autofill path are separate from the missing inline macOS Password AutoFill behavior.

While looking through the Electron source, I found Electron's autofill-related implementation in:
```
shell/renderer/electron_autofill_agent.cc
shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver.cc
shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver_factory.cc
shell/browser/ui/autofill_popup.cc
```
`ElectronAutofillAgent` implements `blink::WebAutofillClient`, but I did not find an obvious integration for macOS Password AutoFill in Electron’s source.

The only `AuthenticationServices` import I found in the Electron source I searched was associated with the macOS platform-passkey implementation:
`shell/browser/webauthn/electron_platform_passkeys_authenticator_mac.mm`

I also searched for:
```
NSTextContentType
AuthenticationServices
ASCredential
current-password
PasswordManagerClient
```
and did not find an obvious bridge for normal username/password AutoFill.

I have not yet built Electron/Chromium from source because I wanted to confirm with maintainers whether this integration belongs in Electron, upstream Chromium, or elsewhere before pursuing an implementation.

</details>

I'm interested in working on an implementation if this is considered in scope for Electron and would appreciate guidance on the appropriate integration point.

(Closest: #10072 from 2017, a different key-prefix problem; #40366 / #40475 concern the WebGL `GPUCache`.) ### Electron Version 42.10.1 (Chromium 148.0.7778.280). The missing override has been missing since Skia's shader cache got its own handle, so every supported version. ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 26200; Intel Iris Xe, driver 30.0.101.1298 (ANGLE / D3D11) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version None. The override has never existed in this repository. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. Chrome and Edge write `User Data\GrShaderCache` and `User Data\ShaderCache` and hit them on the next launch. ### Expected Behavior Shaders that Skia compiles for the display compositor and OOP raster are persisted between launches, like Chrome, so the second launch of an app does not pay for compiling them again. ### Actual Behavior They are never written. Every launch of every Electron app recompiles every shader its UI touches, on the GPU main thread, before the first frame can be presented. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Skia compiles a program
GrShaderCache::store"] --> B["GpuChannelManager::StoreShader
→ StoreBlobToDisk(kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle)"] B --> C{"path registered for
kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle?"} C -->|"Chrome / Edge"| D["ChromeContentBrowserClient::GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory()
→ User Data\\GrShaderCache ✅"] C -->|"Electron"| E["ContentBrowserClient default → empty path
→ no cache for the handle → blob dropped ❌"] ``` - `content/browser/gpu/gpu_disk_cache_factory.cc` maps `kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle` → `GetContentClient()->browser()->GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory()` and `kDisplayCompositorGpuDiskCacheHandle` → `GetShaderDiskCacheDirectory()`, and only registers a cache when the path is non-empty. - `content/public/browser/content_browser_client.cc`: both defaults return `base::FilePath()`. - `shell/browser/electron_browser_client.{h,cc}` override neither (0 hits for `ShaderDiskCache` in this repository). - `gpu/ipc/service/gpu_channel_manager.cc`: `StoreShader` always targets `kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle`, and loads for that handle are the only ones that reach `GrShaderCache::PopulateCache`. The per-renderer `GPUCache` that Electron apps do have feeds `gles2::ProgramCache` (WebGL programs) instead — which is why VS Code's has ~1,200 entries and a non-WebGL app's has 0. Measured on this machine with `--trace-startup` on the first launch of a shell that paints text, rounded rects and shadows, identical on each traced launch: | GPU main thread, first raster of the UI | per launch | |---|---| | `GrShaderCache::load` | 31, all misses | | `GrShaderCache::store` | 31 | | `Program::MainLinkLoadEvent::wait` (ANGLE → `D3DCompile`) | 31 × ~15 ms = **~480 ms**, serialised | | frames presented meanwhile | 0 | | `sessionData/GrShaderCache` after 40 s and a clean exit | does not exist | Same on disk for other apps installed here: | | `GrShaderCache` | `ShaderCache` | `GPUCache` entries | |---|---|---|---| | Chrome, Edge | present | present | (per profile) | | VS Code | absent | absent | 1,223 (WebGL) | | Slack, Discord | absent | absent | present | | this app | absent | absent | 0 | ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/Hona/0ba82a4c26cc576cb4caeebc3f4ec746 — loads a page with a few paint ops, waits 10 s, then prints which shader cache directories exist under `sessionData` and how many entries their index reports. `GrShaderCache` / `ShaderCache` are `absent` on every run; in Chrome the equivalent directories fill up. ### Additional Information Proposed fix, mirroring `ChromeContentBrowserClient`: ```cpp // shell/browser/electron_browser_client.cc base::FilePath ElectronBrowserClient::GetShaderDiskCacheDirectory() { return SessionDataPath().Append(FILE_PATH_LITERAL("ShaderCache")); } base::FilePath ElectronBrowserClient::GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory() { return SessionDataPath().Append(FILE_PATH_LITERAL("GrShaderCache")); } ``` where `SessionDataPath()` is whatever resolves `app.getPath("sessionData")` (the same root the existing `GPUCache` lands in). `GetGraphiteDawnDiskCacheDirectory()` and, on platforms where `features::kGpuPersistentCache` is on, `GetGPUPersistentCacheDirectory()` have the same shape. `session.clearStorageData({ storages: ["shadercache"] })` and the `sessionData` docs would need to cover the new directories. Happy to send the PR.

nodes.title: macOS: setBounds with huge numbers like -1e10 crashes the app
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.2 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 15 (darwin 24.6.0) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Calling `win.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 })` should not crash the app. A bad number should throw a JavaScript error or be ignored. `try/catch` should work. The process should keep running. ### Actual Behavior On macOS the process dies. `setBounds` often returns as if it succeeded. A moment later the app exits with SIGTRAP (133). JavaScript `try/catch` does not catch this. The crash looks like: ``` NSInternalInconsistencyException Invalid parameter not satisfying: CGRectContainsRect( CGRectMake((CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN), frame) self= frame={{-2147483648, ...}, {0, 0}} ``` `-2147483648` is `INT_MIN`. That is not the `-1e10` passed from JavaScript. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/xia-chao/c6d8ef8bb82dea48ae4e1c3260c9234b ### Additional Information How to reproduce on Electron 44.4.2 (macOS arm64): 1. Create a hidden `BaseWindow`. 2. Call `setBounds` with `x` and `y` set to `-1e10` (`-10000000000`). This is a finite number, not `NaN` or `Infinity`. 3. Repeat that call about 40 times. 4. Wait a short time (the assert often fires on a later AppKit tick, after `setBounds` has already returned). ```js const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const w = new BaseWindow({ show: false, width: 400, height: 300 }); for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) { w.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 }); } setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 800); }); ``` Fix in progress: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/54101 **1. Breakpoint at `ToRoundedRect`. Locals already show `x` / `y` = `-1e+10`.** **2. Call stack: JS `setBounds` is inside the C++ rect converter.** **3. Debug console: normal bounds first, then the trigger `-10000000000`.** **4. After continue: AppKit asserts on an `INT_MIN` frame, process SIGTRAP.**
In-depth investigation

On Electron 44.4.2, `gin::Converter::FromV8` calls `ToRoundedRect`. A finite value like `-1e10` saturates to `INT_MIN` on float-to-int conversion. `NativeWindowMac::SetBounds` clamps size, not origin, then calls `[window_ setFrame:]`. AppKit asserts and the process dies. An `isfinite`-only check would still accept `-1e10`.

### Electron Version

44.4.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15 (darwin 24.6.0, arm64)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown. Reproduced on Electron 44.4.2.

### Expected Behavior

`win.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 })` should not crash the process.

A bad number should either throw a JavaScript error, or be ignored. `try/catch` should be enough. The app should keep running.

### Actual Behavior

On macOS the **whole app dies**.

`setBounds` often returns as if nothing happened. A moment later AppKit asserts and the process exits with **SIGTRAP (133)**. JavaScript `try/catch` cannot catch this.

The crash message looks like:

```
NSInternalInconsistencyException
Invalid parameter not satisfying: CGRectContainsRect(
  CGRectMake((CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MIN,
             (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN,
             (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN), frame)
self=<ElectronNSWindow> frame={{-2147483648, ...}, {0, 0}}
```

`-2147483648` is `INT_MIN`. That is not the `-1e10` we passed from JavaScript.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/xia-chao/c6d8ef8bb82dea48ae4e1c3260c9234b

### Additional Information

## 用大白话说发生了什么

1. 我建了一个隐藏的 `BaseWindow`。
2. 我调用 `setBounds`，把窗口坐标写成 `-10000000000`（也就是 `-1e10`）。这个数还是有限数，不是 `NaN`，也不是 `Infinity`。
3. Electron 把这个浮点数转成 C++ 的 `int` 时溢出了，结果变成最小整数 `-2147483648`。
4. 这个超大负数被交给 macOS 设窗口位置。AppKit 检查「窗口必须落在允许范围内」，检查失败就直接把进程干掉。
5. 所以这不是「窗口跑出屏幕」那么简单，是**原生层崩了**。

只检查 `NaN` / `Infinity` **挡不住这次崩溃**。`-1e10` 是普通有限数字，照样能把 `int` 撑爆。

## 怎么稳定复现

环境：Electron **44.4.2**，macOS arm64。

```js
const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const w = new BaseWindow({ show: false, width: 400, height: 300 });
  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
    w.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 });
  }
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 800);
});
```

断言经常在 `setBounds` **返回之后**的下一次 AppKit 事件循环才炸。多写几次更容易撞上。

## 调试截图（源码断点）

调试的是官方 **v44.4.2** 的 `gfx_converter.cc`：`Converter<gfx::Rect>::FromV8` 里调用 `ToRoundedRect` 那一行。

**图 1：断在转换代码上。变量里 `x` / `y` 已经是 `-1e+10`。**

![source breakpoint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/electron-setbounds-intmin-20260919/electron/setbounds-intmin/01-source-breakpoint.png)

**图 2：调用栈。JS 的 `setBounds` 已经进到 C++ 的矩形转换。**

![call stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/electron-setbounds-intmin-20260919/electron/setbounds-intmin/02-call-stack.png)

**图 3：调试控制台。先打印正常窗口位置，再打印触发值 `-10000000000`。**

![debug console](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/electron-setbounds-intmin-20260919/electron/setbounds-intmin/03-debug-console.png)

**图 4：继续跑之后的崩溃。AppKit 报 `INT_MIN` 窗口 frame，进程 SIGTRAP。**

![appkit crash](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/electron-setbounds-intmin-20260919/electron/setbounds-intmin/04-appkit-crash.png)

## 代码路径（给对过源码的人）

`gin::Converter<gfx::Rect>::FromV8` → `ToRoundedRect(gfx::RectF(...))` saturates float→int to `INT_MIN`.

`NativeWindowMac::SetBounds` clamps size, not origin, then `[window_ setFrame:]`.

This is a successor to the earlier `isfinite`-only idea: that check would still let `-1e10` through.

I will send a PR that rejects non-finite **and** out-of-int-range values and throws a JS error instead of crashing.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, GNOME 46 (Mutter), **Wayland** session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), linux-arm64 (Parallels VM) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version 42.x — Linux windows had no rounding at all before 43, so a framed window was square on all four corners and there was no visible mismatch. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior A window's four corners should be consistent with each other. On macOS and Windows the same window configuration renders rounded corners on all four corners, so I would expect framed windows on Linux to either be rounded on all four corners as well, or square on all four — not mixed. For reference, `frame: false` on the same machine renders rounded corners on all four corners correctly. ### Actual Behavior On Linux (Wayland), a `BrowserWindow` created with `frame: true` renders **rounded top corners and square bottom corners**. The top and bottom of the window visibly do not match, because the top corners follow the CSD frame's rounding while the content area below keeps square corners. No error is thrown and nothing appears in the console — the window simply draws with an asymmetric shape. Steps: 1. Open the gist from the Testcase Gist URL below in [Electron Fiddle](https://github.com/electron/fiddle), or download it and run `npx electron .` in the folder. It opens one framed and one frameless window side by side. 2. Look at the four corners of each window. The framed window: rounded at the top, square at the bottom. The frameless window: rounded on all four corners. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/DeJeune/6f71a14df8cfd9d8cd16438c1a0d9359 ### Additional Information I am not sure whether this is intended, so the main question is: **is a framed window on Linux supposed to have consistent corners, and if so which way?** If the current mixed shape is intended, then it would help to document it — the `roundedCorners` option is documented as applying to *frameless* windows only ("Whether a frameless window should have rounded corners"), which suggests an app has no supported way to influence the corners of a framed window at all. Extra environment detail, in case the desktop matters: this is native Wayland on GNOME 46 / Mutter, not XWayland.
In-depth investigation

Context that may be useful once someone picks this up — I deliberately kept it out of the sections above. **Where the rounding comes from** - The frameless path is fine and is what the release notes describe: Electron 43 added "Frameless windows on Linux now have rounded corners by default" ([#52111](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/52111), also [#51459](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51459)). That path deliberately scoped itself to frameless windows. - The framed path is a different code path. [`#51160`](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51160) "refactor: replace ClientFrameViewLinux with NativeFrameViewLinux" (merged 2026-04-28) replaced the Linux client frame view with a thin wrapper over Chromium's `views::NativeFrameViewLinux`. That is the code that draws the frame for `frame: true` on Linux, and it is where the top-only rounding appears to come from. - I could not find an existing report for the framed case. The closest open issue I found is [#52024](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/52024) ("Linux: frameless windows have a border on non-compositing X11 WMs"), which is about the frameless path on X11 and not this symptom. **Why I did not just work around it in my app** - `roundedCorners` is documented as frameless-only: > `roundedCorners` boolean (optional) - Whether a frameless window should have rounded corners. Default is `true`. ... On Linux, rounded corners are only drawn when the desktop environment supports client-side decorations. - I verified it is a no-op for a framed window: `frame: true` and `frame: true, roundedCorners: false` produce an identical window on this machine, while `frame: false` vs `frame: false, roundedCorners: false` visibly differ (four rounded corners vs four square corners). So the only app-side lever would be to force the *frameless* look square, which would make Linux diverge from macOS/Windows rather than fix anything. **Related docs** - `win.setBounds` / `win.setPosition` / `win.getBounds`: "On Wayland (Linux), has the same limitations as ..." / "On Wayland, this method will return `{ x: 0, y: 0, ... }` as introspecting or programmatically changing the global window coordinates is prohibited." — mentioned only because it confirms Wayland is treated as a distinct path in this area, not because I think it is related to the corners.

### Expected Behavior

A `type: 'panel'` window should accept clicks without activating the app. After switching to another app, clicking a button in the panel should run the button's handler and leave the other app active.

### Actual Behavior

Clicking the button makes Electron the active app instead. Electron emits `did-become-active`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/danteissaias/5334864f77f77f3b099f408c66d3346b

3. Click the panel's “Click me” button.
4. Notice that the button text changes, but Electron also becomes active. The console logs `did-become-active`.

### Additional Information

I found a workaround, but it requires a rather horrible private AppKit API. A small native addon calls this method on the panel before it is shown:

```objc
[window _setPreventsActivation:YES];
```

With this call, the button still works and the previous app stays active. Clicking the panel no longer emits `did-become-active`.

nodes.title: Calling setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false) during macOS window blur can crash the main process
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a matching bug report without success. ### Electron Version 44.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown. Older versions of the application did not execute this API call during the same window-blur path. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. `webContents.setIgnoreMenuShortcuts()` is an Electron-specific API. ### Expected Behavior Calling `webContents.setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false)` while a `BrowserWindow` is losing focus should update the shortcut state safely, or have no effect when shortcuts are already enabled. The Electron main process should remain running. ### Actual Behavior The Electron main process intermittently terminates with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)` during a macOS window-focus transition. The crash was observed repeatedly when `browser-window-blur` synchronously caused `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false)` to be called for multiple `webContents` instances, including `BrowserWindow`, `WebContentsView`, and detached DevTools contents. After a crash, macOS window-state restoration can immediately restore the same window arrangement and cause a crash loop on subsequent development launches. Seven same-signature crashes were recorded with Electron 44.2.0 during one investigation session. A matching crash was also observed with Electron 43.4.1. ### Testcase Gist URL A standalone testcase is not currently available. An attempted reduced example using two `BrowserWindow`s, a `WebContentsView`, detached DevTools, and automatic focus changes did not reproduce the crash reliably. ### Additional Information Adding an application-side state guard stopped the crash: `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false)` is now called only if a shortcut hold was actually active. Ordinary window blur events no longer perform an idempotent native reset, and the guarded behavior has automated regression coverage. On macOS, launching the development application once with `-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES` bypassed the window-state restoration loop. This is only a recovery measure. Issue #53808 also concerns a `WebContentsView` native crash, but has a different trigger: it passes an extension background page into `new WebContentsView({ webContents })` and crashes while applying web preferences. This report concerns `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false)` during an AppKit focus transition. Sanitized crash summary: ```text Application: Electron Electron version: 44.2.0 Operating system: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84) Architecture: arm64 Translated: No Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000110 Termination Reason: SIGNAL 11, Segmentation fault Faulting Thread: CrBrowserMain Dispatch Queue: com.apple.main-thread Relevant partially symbolicated frames: -[NSWindow _realMakeFirstResponder:] + 196 -[NSView _setHidden:setNeedsDisplay:] + 280 ```
In-depth investigation

The application originally attached a reset callback for every `webContents` created, including BrowserWindow renderers, WebContentsViews, and detached DevTools: ```js app.on("web-contents-created", (_event, contents) => { const reset = () => { if (!contents.isDestroyed()) { contents.setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false); } }; app.on("browser-window-blur", reset); contents.once("destroyed", () => { app.removeListener("browser-window-blur", reset); }); }); ``` Consequently, one `browser-window-blur` event could synchronously update several native views while AppKit was changing the first responder. The application-side mitigation avoids the native call unless the state was previously enabled: ```js const reset = () => { if (!held) return; held = undefined; if (!contents.isDestroyed()) { contents.setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false); } }; ``` The correlation with `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts(false)` and the effectiveness of the state guard are strong, but a standalone testcase has not yet reproduced the failure reliably. The surrounding Electron frames were not symbolicated reliably enough to identify a specific Electron source location.

Both `menu.popup({ window, sourceType: 'mouse' })` and `menu.popup(win)` show it. nodes.title: Windows MSIX/AppX: GPU process killed when Code Integrity rejects an externally-injected DLL (Auto Super Resolution), not an app-bundled one
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home, build 10.0.26200, ARM64

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

An MSIX/AppX-packaged Electron application should initialize its GPU process
successfully even when a third-party DLL injected into that process by the
operating system fails the GPU child's binary-signature policy.

If an injected module cannot be loaded under the GPU process's Code Integrity
policy, the load failure should be non-fatal — as it is for the same DLL in
non-packaged Chromium processes on the same machine — rather than terminating the
GPU process and, after the retry limit, the entire application.

### Actual Behavior

This is a distinct trigger from #52700, and it contradicts the packaging-defect
conclusion reached in that thread.

In every report on #52700 the rejected DLL is `vk_swiftshader.dll`, bundled
*inside* the application package — so the app's own signing and Code Integrity
catalog are plausibly at fault, and the assessment there concluded this was
"primarily a packaging defect."

In this report the rejected DLL is **`SuperResExt.dll`, shipped by Microsoft in a
separate MSIX package** (`Microsoft.AutoSuperResolution`) and injected into the
GPU child from outside the application entirely. The affected applications'
signing, catalogs and page hashes are irrelevant to it. **No amount of correct
application packaging can prevent this failure.**

## Mechanism

On Copilot+ ARM64 hardware, Windows Auto Super Resolution injects
`SuperResExt.dll` into Chromium-based processes. In MSIX-packaged Electron apps
the GPU child runs with `MicrosoftSignedOnly`; the injected DLL does not satisfy
it; Code Integrity logs Event 3033 and the GPU process is killed. Chromium
respawns it, the identical rejection recurs, and the app aborts at the retry
limit.

Because injection happens at launch, **the app never draws a window** — no error
dialog, no in-app recovery, and on MSIX no way for a user to pass a mitigating
flag.

## Two unrelated MSIX Electron apps affected; non-MSIX control unaffected

| App | Packaging | Arch | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Desktop 1.52386.3.0 | MSIX | arm64 native | Dies at launch |
| Proton Pass 1.40.0.0 | MSIX | x64 under Prism emulation | Dies at launch |
| VS Code (arm64) | **non-MSIX**, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` | arm64 native | **Works**, GPU sandbox enabled |

Different vendors, different Electron versions, different architectures. The only
shared property is MSIX packaging.

## The rejection is routine machine-wide — only MSIX makes it fatal

Event 3033 counts for `SuperResExt.dll` over a 2-day window on this machine:

| Process | Event 3033 count | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `msedgewebview2.exe` | 112 | Works |
| `claude.exe` | 36 | **Dies** |
| `ProtonPass.exe` | 27 | **Dies** |
| `msedge.exe` | 4 | Works |
| `Code.exe` | 1 | Works |

Edge, WebView2 and VS Code take the same rejection of the same DLL, in the same
sessions, and carry on normally. This also answers the Chrome/Chromium question:
the rejection occurs there too, the fatality does not.

## Crash signature

    Claude Desktop:
      ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1017]
        GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=101457950
      ... to 6 crashes ...
      FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:418]
        GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.

    Proton Pass:
      ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:999]
        GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=101457950
      ... to 9 crashes ...
      FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415]
        GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.

    exit_code 101457950 = 0x060C201E — same code as #52700 and the Codex reports

Code Integrity event (`Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational`), verbatim:

    Code Integrity determined that a process (\Device\HarddiskVolume14\Program
    Files\WindowsApps\Claude_1.52386.3.0_arm64__pzs8sxrjxfjjc\app\claude.exe)
    attempted to load \Device\HarddiskVolume14\Program Files\WindowsApps\
    Microsoft.AutoSuperResolution_1.0.1.0_arm64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\SuperResExt.dll
    that did not meet the Microsoft signing level requirements.

One Event 3033 plus three Event 3089 per GPU child spawn attempt, second-aligned
with each crash. Identical event text for `ProtonPass.exe`.

**Note:** `vk_swiftshader.dll` (5.0.0) IS present in the Claude Desktop package,
but it was NOT rejected in this reproduction — no Event 3033 names it, and no
Event 3010 (missing `CodeIntegrity.cat`) appears. The only rejected module is the
externally-injected `SuperResExt.dll`. The app ships the binary implicated in
#52700, Code Integrity accepted it, and the crash originated elsewhere.

## A/B test — three states, same machine

| ASR state | `claude.exe` 3033 events | Claude Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Package registered (Windows default) | 36 | Dies at launch |
| Toggled **Off** in Settings, rebooted | 12 | Dies at launch |
| Package **removed**, rebooted | 0 | **Launches normally** |

After removal both apps launch from their Start Menu tiles with no flags and the
GPU sandbox fully enabled. The Windows Settings toggle does not stop injection,
so the only user-available mitigation is removing a Microsoft OS component.

## Flag bisect — eliminates the graphics stack

| Flag | Result |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | Crash |
| `--use-angle=d3d11-warp` | **Crash** |
| `--in-process-gpu` | Works, hardware acceleration intact |
| `--disable-gpu-sandbox` | Works, hardware acceleration intact |

WARP is Microsoft's CPU software rasteriser and does not touch the vendor GPU
path, so the crash surviving it rules out the GPU driver and the ANGLE D3D11
rendering path. Both working flags eliminate the *restricted child process*
rather than changing rendering, localising the fault to GPU child creation under
the signing policy.

## Ruled out

- **GPU driver** — identical on current Qualcomm UGD 31.0.152.1; survives WARP. `anthropics/claude-code#68049` reports identical failure on an older OEM driver on comparable hardware.
- **Orphaned/zombie SID DACLs (#51761)** — `%LOCALAPPDATA%` DACL clean (SYSTEM, Administrators, user only; no orphaned `S-1-15-2-*`). Both failing packages' DACLs are equivalent to Windows Terminal, Notepad and Proton Pass; `S-1-15-2-2` is absent from **all** of them including the working ones, so its absence is not the differentiator on this platform.
- **App package signing/catalog** — `Get-AppxPackage` Status: Ok for both; the rejected DLL is in neither package.
- **Qualcomm Snapdragon/Adreno Control Panel** — uninstalled, rebooted, no change.
- **Exploit Protection** — `Get-ProcessMitigation -System`: every mitigation `NOTSET`, no overrides.
- **WER** — no Application Error/Hang entry; no Display/Dxgkrnl TDR events at any crash timestamp.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Environment:
  Device:       ASUS Zenbook A14 UX3407QA
  SoC:          Qualcomm Snapdragon X X1-26-100 (ARM64, Copilot+)
  GPU:          Qualcomm Adreno X1-45, driver 31.0.152.1 (2026-05-23,
                Qualcomm Upgradeable Graphics Driver)
  OS:           Windows 11 Home, build 10.0.26200, ARM64
  Device Guard: HVCI + System Guard Secure Launch active
                (SecurityServicesRunning {2,3})
  Exploit Prot: all system mitigations NOTSET, no overrides

Electron version: not determinable from the shipped MSIX builds. Both vendors
overwrite the executable's version metadata with their own app version
(claude.exe reports 1.52386.3; ProtonPass.exe reports 1.40.0), and the bundled
Chromium DLLs carry no usable Chromium version string. The two affected apps
clearly bundle different Electron versions, evidenced by the differing source
line numbers in the crash output above (gpu_process_host.cc:1017 vs :999,
gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:418 vs :415) — which also indicates the failure
is not specific to one Electron version.

Claude Desktop auto-updated from 1.46388.4.0 to 1.52386.3.0 during this
investigation; the crash reproduced identically on both builds. The source line
numbers above correspond to the build bundled with 1.46388.4.0.

Relationship to existing reports:
  electron/electron#52700 — same fatality mechanism (MSIX + CIG rejection kills
    the GPU child), different trigger. The rejected DLL here is injected by the
    OS from a separate package rather than bundled in the app, which the
    packaging-defect explanation in that thread does not cover.
  electron/electron#51761 — different root cause (orphaned SID DACLs), ruled out
    here.
  anthropics/claude-code#68049 — same device class and exit code, closed as
    invalid for want of this root cause; that reporter could not test any flags
    because direct exe launch from WindowsApps was ACL-blocked.
  anthropics/claude-code#81341 — same CIG mechanism, bundled vk_swiftshader.dll.
  openai/codex#34133 — Event 3033, Status 0xC0000428, RequestedPolicy 8,
    ValidatedPolicy 1, then exitCode 101457950.

Also filed with Microsoft via Feedback Hub, since Auto Super Resolution, the
signing policy, and the failing binary are all Microsoft-side:
https://aka.ms/AA13dw5h (opens in the Windows Feedback Hub app)

Diagnosability note: the surfaced symptom is a bare GPU-process exit code with no
module name anywhere in the Electron log. The Code Integrity event log is the only
place the cause appears, and nothing points a user toward it. Logging the rejected
module on GPU child launch failure would stop this class of bug being
misattributed to graphics drivers — which is what happened in
anthropics/claude-code#68049.

### Expected Behavior

Hello :-)

When running Paper Desktop it's very common to tab back and fourth between your IDE and Paper itself when using Paper MCP. Because of this the behaviour in Wayland causes frames to stop being ran until focus is back in the window. This ends up blocking anything requiring an animation loop, for Paper that's screenshots and exports.

It looks like [Chromium ran into this](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/de4b707490acca3612e077adaa35679231ee4b35) and shipped a workaround for WebRTC which we end up leaning on: starting self capture for the view so frames continue firing even when the window is occluded.

On macOS/Windows it's enough to disable background throttling, for Linux Wayland that's not the case and we needed to reach for self capture.

The deprecated and now removed APIs `webContents.incrementCapturerCount` / `decrementCapturerCount` sounded like they could have also solved this problem.

### Actual Behavior

When an Electron window / view is occluded frames stop firing, even with background throttling being disabled.
